claims.text: ADAM8 is reported higher in TNBC/basal-like tumours and linked to invasion and brain metastasis.
ADAM8 is not a broad CRISPR dependency in breast lines.
Only preclinical ADAM8 inhibitors and antibodies exist, with no breast cancer trial.

dossier.rationale: ADAM8 has a plausible role in invasion in TNBC, but it lacks a growth dependency and clinical-stage drugs. Evidence is preclinical and mostly correlative.

claims.text: RRP1B is a germline metastasis-susceptibility modifier, with a context-dependent role in tumour progression.
It is not a strong dependency in basal lines.
No drug against RRP1B has been tested in clinical trials.

dossier.rationale: RRP1B is mainly a metastasis-modifier gene with no drug and no clear dependency. It is a poor target.

claims.text: SRPK1 is upregulated in breast tumours versus normal tissue.
SRPK1 shows moderate dependency in some breast lines.
SRPK1 inhibitors such as SPHINX31 are preclinical, and none has reached a breast cancer trial.
SRPK1 is broadly expressed in normal tissues.

dossier.rationale: SRPK1 is a druggable kinase with oncogenic splicing roles. Its expression is broad and it has no breast trials yet.

claims.text: CDC123 is a common-essential gene needed for eIF2 assembly.
It is ubiquitously expressed.
No drug against CDC123 has been tested clinically.

dossier.rationale: CDC123 is an essential housekeeping gene, so there is no therapeutic window. No drugs exist against it.

claims.text: CDCA8, a chromosomal passenger complex member, is a proliferation gene highly expressed in basal-like tumours.
CDCA8 is commonly essential in CRISPR screens.
No CDCA8-specific drug exists, though Aurora B inhibitors in the same complex have been trialled.
CDCA8 expression is low in most non-proliferating normal tissues.

dossier.rationale: CDCA8 is strongly proliferation-linked and basal-enriched but essential in all dividing cells. It has no direct drug.

claims.text: PRPF3 is a core spliceosome gene and is commonly essential.
It is not specifically elevated in basal-like tumours.
No PRPF3 drug exists.

dossier.rationale: PRPF3 is a housekeeping spliceosome component. It is essential and not subtype-selective.

claims.text: VDR is not higher in basal-like tumours than in other breast tumours, and is often lower.
VDR knockout does not reduce growth of basal lines.
Calcitriol and vitamin D analogues have been trialled in breast cancer, mainly as agonists.
VDR is widely expressed in normal tissues.

dossier.rationale: VDR has clinical history only as an agonist, and cell lines do not depend on it. Evidence for a basal-specific benefit is weak.

claims.text: PHLDA2 is an imprinted gene, with variable and context-dependent expression in tumours.
PHLDA2 is not a growth dependency.
No drug exists.

dossier.rationale: PHLDA2 is a small imprinted regulator with no dependency and no druggable mechanism. Its score is low.

claims.text: METTL13, a translation-elongation methyltransferase, is reported upregulated in some cancers.
The dependency in breast lines is weak or variable.
No drug has entered trials.

dossier.rationale: METTL13 is a methyltransferase with modest cancer links and no clinical-stage compounds. The case is speculative.

claims.text: E2F3 is higher in basal-like tumours, which have RB1 loss and cell-cycle activation, and is sometimes amplified.
E2F3 shows some dependency, but E2F family redundancy limits it.
There are no direct E2F inhibitors in trials.

dossier.rationale: E2F3 is a transcription factor that is elevated in basal-like disease. It is hard to drug and partly redundant.

claims.text: NCAPD2, a condensin I subunit, tracks with proliferation and is higher in basal-like tumours.
It is commonly essential.
No drug against condensin has entered trials.

dossier.rationale: NCAPD2 is basal-enriched and essential, but it is a general proliferation factor without a drug. The therapeutic window is narrow.

claims.text: ANP32E, an H2A.Z chaperone, is higher in basal-like and TNBC tumours and is linked to poor prognosis.
It is not a strong dependency in most lines.
No drug exists.

dossier.rationale: ANP32E is basal-enriched with prognostic associations. Its dependency evidence is weak and it is not druggable now.

claims.text: MBOAT7 is a lipid-remodelling acyltransferase studied mostly in liver disease.
It is not a dependency in breast lines.
No breast cancer drug exists.

dossier.rationale: MBOAT7 has little breast cancer rationale. There is no dependency and no drug.

claims.text: FLVCR1 is a choline transporter that is a dependency in some lines, depending on choline supply.
It is broadly expressed in normal tissues.
No drug exists.

dossier.rationale: FLVCR1 is a transporter with some metabolic dependency in cell lines. It is broadly expressed and has no clinical compounds.

claims.text: SUV39H2, an H3K9 methyltransferase, is modestly elevated in proliferative tumours.
It is not an essential gene in breast lines.
SUV39 inhibitors such as chaetocin have not reached breast cancer trials.

dossier.rationale: SUV39H2 is a plausible epigenetic target, but no dependency or clinical-grade inhibitor supports it.

claims.text: BCL-XL knockout reduces growth in many TNBC/basal lines, which rely on BCL-XL for survival.
Navitoclax (BCL-2/BCL-XL/BCL-W) and the BCL-XL degrader DT2216 have been tested in solid tumours including breast.
BCL2L1 is higher in breast tumours, and 20q11 gain is common.
BCL-XL is needed in platelets and is broadly expressed, causing thrombocytopenia.

dossier.rationale: BCL2L1 is one of the better-supported genes here, with real dependency in basal lines and clinical-stage drugs. Platelet toxicity limits it.

claims.text: HMGA1 is highly expressed in basal-like and TNBC tumours and is linked to poor outcome.
It is higher in tumours than in normal breast.
Dependency is modest and variable.
No direct HMGA1 drug has been trialled.

dossier.rationale: HMGA1 is a basal-enriched oncofetal chromatin factor. It is poorly druggable and its dependency is inconsistent.

claims.text: STK4 (MST1) is a Hippo pathway kinase with tumour-suppressive function.
Knockout does not reduce growth.
No inhibitor has been trialled in breast cancer.

dossier.rationale: STK4 acts mainly as a tumour suppressor, so inhibiting it is the wrong direction for treatment. Its score is very low.

claims.text: CDCA2 (Repo-Man) is a proliferation gene higher in basal-like tumours.
It is not consistently essential.
Its normal tissue expression is low outside proliferating cells.
No drug exists.

dossier.rationale: CDCA2 is basal-enriched and tumour-restricted in expression. Dependency is weak and there is no drug.

claims.text: TMEM165 is a Golgi Ca/Mn transporter involved in glycosylation.
It is not a dependency in breast lines.
No drug exists.

dossier.rationale: TMEM165 is a housekeeping transporter with no oncology case. There is no dependency or drug.

claims.text: Peroxisomal transporter, not a recognised dependency in breast lines.
No drug against ABCD3 has reached breast cancer trials.

dossier.rationale: Peroxisomal fatty acid transporter with no known subtype-specific role. No dependency or drug evidence, so a very weak target.

claims.text: SUMO E2 enzyme UBC9 is broadly essential in cell lines.
No clear HER2-enriched-specific upregulation.
SUMOylation inhibitors (e.g. TAK-981 targets SAE) are not UBE2I-directed in breast trials.

dossier.rationale: Pan-essential gene, so dependency is likely but not selective. Narrow therapeutic window and no subtype enrichment limit it.

claims.text: Deubiquitinase with little evidence of essentiality in breast lines.
No clinical-stage OTUB2 drug.

dossier.rationale: Limited evidence of a role in HER2-enriched disease. Not a credible target on present knowledge.

claims.text: Mitochondrial aspartyl-tRNA synthetase, modest or no dependency.
No clinical drug.

dossier.rationale: Housekeeping mitochondrial translation gene without subtype selectivity. Weak target.

claims.text: CSN5/JAB1 is upregulated in several tumours including breast.
Commonly essential in cell lines.
CSN5 inhibitors are preclinical.

dossier.rationale: Plausible oncogenic role and broad dependency, but not subtype-specific and no clinical drug. Modest target.

claims.text: Not a strong dependency in breast lines.
No clinical drug.

dossier.rationale: Chromatin remodeler with little subtype-specific evidence. Weak target.

claims.text: Mitochondrial chaperone, dependency known mainly in AML.
No clinical drug in breast cancer.

dossier.rationale: Interest is mainly in AML. Little evidence for HER2-enriched breast cancer.

claims.text: Importin beta-1 is broadly essential.
Elevated in many tumours.
Importazole and similar compounds are preclinical.

dossier.rationale: Common-essential gene with tumour upregulation, giving a limited therapeutic window. No clinical precedent.

claims.text: V-ATPase subunits are commonly essential.
Ubiquitously expressed.

dossier.rationale: V-ATPase subunit that is ubiquitous and broadly essential. Toxicity concerns and no subtype selectivity.

claims.text: Amplified and overexpressed by definition in HER2-enriched tumours.
Much higher than in normal breast.
HER2-amplified lines are strongly dependent on ERBB2.
Trastuzumab, pertuzumab, T-DXd, tucatinib, lapatinib are approved.

dossier.rationale: The defining driver and validated target. Reference point for the scale.

claims.text: No known HER2-enriched association.
Not essential in breast lines.

dossier.rationale: Kinesin with little evidence in breast cancer. Weak target.

claims.text: Co-amplified with ERBB2 on 17q12 and strongly overexpressed.
Higher in HER2+ tumours than normal breast.
Dependency is modest and probably confounded by ERBB2 co-amplification.
No GRB7 drug in trials.

dossier.rationale: Strong biomarker of the amplicon with a signalling adaptor role. Little proof of independent dependency and no drugs.

claims.text: Reported as a tumour suppressor in breast cancer.
No drug.

dossier.rationale: Literature suggests a tumour-suppressive role, so inhibition is unattractive.

claims.text: ESCRT-III component with weak breast dependency evidence.
No drug.

dossier.rationale: ESCRT component without subtype link or druggability. Weak target.

claims.text: Pol I initiation factor, commonly essential.
Pol I inhibitors (CX-5461) act through other mechanisms.

dossier.rationale: Ribosomal DNA transcription is a cancer vulnerability, but RRN3 is not subtype-specific and has no direct drug.

claims.text: Golgin, not an essential gene in breast lines.
No drug.

dossier.rationale: No evidence of a role in HER2-enriched disease. Not a target.

claims.text: Located at 17q21 near ERBB2 and often co-amplified and upregulated in HER2+ tumours.
Proteasome regulatory subunit, commonly essential.
Proteasome inhibitors target catalytic subunits, not PSMD3.

dossier.rationale: Amplicon-linked and broadly essential, but this is likely a passenger co-amplification and a pan-essential gene. Modest score.

claims.text: Capivasertib (approved in HR+ disease) and ipatasertib have been trialled in breast cancer.
Partial dependency in HER2-amplified lines, buffered by AKT2.
Activity is driven by pathway signalling, not mRNA enrichment.

dossier.rationale: Downstream HER2 effector with clinical-stage inhibitors. Redundancy with AKT2 and limited subtype specificity temper the score.

claims.text: Proline biosynthesis enzyme P5CS, upregulated in some cancers.
No drug.

dossier.rationale: Metabolic enzyme with some preclinical interest. No subtype evidence or drug.

claims.text: Adjacent to ERBB2 on 17q12 and co-amplified in HER2+ tumours.
HER2-amplified lines show sensitivity to CDK12 loss or inhibition.
Selective CDK12 inhibitors are preclinical or early phase; dinaciclib is non-selective.

dossier.rationale: Co-amplified with ERBB2 with preclinical dependency and combination rationale with PARP or HER2 inhibitors. Clinical development is early.

claims.text: FAF2 is not a common essential or luminal-selective dependency.
No FAF2-directed drug has entered breast cancer trials.

dossier.rationale: ER-stress and lipid-droplet protein with no known luminal-specific role. No drugs or selective dependency. Weak target.

claims.text: HNRNPL is a broadly essential splicing factor, so knockout likely reduces growth.
HNRNPL is ubiquitously expressed in normal tissues.
No HNRNPL drug has reached breast cancer trials.

dossier.rationale: Pan-essential RNA-binding protein, so the dependency is not selective for luminal disease. Ubiquitous expression predicts toxicity. Low score.

claims.text: C1orf122 is poorly characterised and not a known dependency.
No drug exists.

dossier.rationale: Uncharacterised mitochondrial-associated gene with no evidence for a role in luminal cancer. No therapeutic precedent.

claims.text: CCDC125 is not known to be required for breast line growth.
No drug exists.

dossier.rationale: Poorly characterised coiled-coil protein linked to motility. No luminal dependency or drug.

claims.text: TADA1 is a SAGA component with modest dependency in some lines.
No TADA1 drug has reached breast cancer trials.

dossier.rationale: Chromatin-modifying complex subunit with no subtype specificity. Hard to drug.

claims.text: RHOC is associated with invasion and metastasis in breast tumours.
RHOC knockout does not strongly reduce growth in luminal lines.
No RHOC-specific drug has reached breast cancer trials.

dossier.rationale: Metastasis-related small GTPase that is not a growth dependency. Difficult to drug directly. Low score.

claims.text: FAAH is not required for breast line growth.
FAAH inhibitors were tested in pain and anxiety, not breast cancer.

dossier.rationale: Endocannabinoid-degrading enzyme with no oncogenic dependency. Existing inhibitors target neurological indications.

claims.text: DDX54 is an essential ribosome-biogenesis helicase.
DDX54 is expressed broadly in normal tissues.

dossier.rationale: Common-essential helicase, so growth dependency is not selective. No clinical precedence and a narrow therapeutic window.

claims.text: MCCC2 is reported as upregulated in some tumours.
Leucine catabolism is generally non-essential in culture.
No drug has been tested.

dossier.rationale: Mitochondrial leucine-catabolism enzyme. Metabolic role is plausible but dependency is weak and there are no drugs.

claims.text: PP2A catalytic subunit is broadly essential.
PP2A inhibitors (LB-100) reached trials in other cancers, with little precedent in breast.
PPP2CA is ubiquitous.

dossier.rationale: PP2A is a tumour suppressor complex and is ubiquitous, so inhibiting it carries toxicity risk. Not subtype-selective.

claims.text: HSP110 is elevated in many tumours.
HSPH1 has a modest dependency effect, partly buffered by other chaperones.
No HSPH1 drug has reached breast cancer trials.

dossier.rationale: Chaperone upregulated in cancer but redundant with other HSPs. No clinical-stage agents.

claims.text: Nucleostemin is commonly essential for proliferation.
GNL3 is higher in proliferating tumour tissue.
No drug exists.

dossier.rationale: Nucleolar GTPase tied to proliferation. Broad essentiality and no drugs limit its value.

claims.text: Condensin subunit NCAPG is strongly upregulated in breast tumours.
It tracks proliferation and is higher in high-grade luminal B tumours.
Condensin loss impairs mitosis in cell lines.
No condensin inhibitor has reached breast trials.

dossier.rationale: Proliferation marker with plausible mitotic dependency, but it is not luminal-specific and has no drugs. Moderate-low score.

claims.text: GATA3 is a luminal lineage marker, high in ER+ tumours.
Luminal lines such as MCF7 and T47D depend on GATA3.
No GATA3-directed drug has reached breast trials, though a GATA3 antisense agent was tested in asthma.
GATA3 is expressed in T cells, kidney and other tissues.

dossier.rationale: Strong luminal lineage dependency, but transcription factors are hard to drug and the gene is expressed outside breast. It is also often a favourable prognostic marker.

claims.text: eIF2 beta is a common-essential translation factor.
EIF2S2 is ubiquitous.

dossier.rationale: Core translation initiation subunit with pan-essential dependency, so selectivity and therapeutic window are poor.

claims.text: PCYOX1L is not required for growth.
No drug exists.

dossier.rationale: Prenylcysteine oxidase-like enzyme with no oncology role established. Weak target.

claims.text: FOXA1 is higher in ER+ luminal tumours and is an ER pioneer factor.
Luminal lines depend on FOXA1 for ER programmes and growth.
No FOXA1-directed drug has reached trials.
FOXA1 is expressed in liver, prostate and other tissues.

dossier.rationale: Best-supported luminal dependency of this set, with a link to endocrine resistance. It is a pioneer transcription factor with no drug and no tissue restriction.

claims.text: BLZF1 (Golgin-45) is not a growth dependency.
No drug exists.

dossier.rationale: Golgi structural protein with no cancer dependency evidence.

claims.text: JNK2 knockout does not strongly reduce luminal line growth.
JNK inhibitors have reached early clinical trials in other diseases, with little precedent in breast.

dossier.rationale: Stress kinase that is druggable in principle, but isoform redundancy and context-dependent roles weaken the case. No luminal dependency.

claims.text: CXXC5 is estrogen-induced and higher in ER+ tumours.
It is not a strong growth dependency.
No drug exists.

dossier.rationale: ER-associated marker and transcription regulator. Subtype enrichment is real but dependency is weak and it is hard to drug.
